prompts: A client loves the woodblock print attached, also in {WS}/print.jpg; it is in the public domain. They want a 3D wallpaper that copies it: its composition, its palette and its subjects, so anyone who knows the print recognizes it at a glance, rebuilt as our own low poly scene with some gentle motion. Deliver {WS}/scene/index.html, a single file with everything built in code: the print is the reference, not a texture. Record in {WS}/result.json what you took from it: boats (how many the print shows) and mountain (its name). It is reviewed by opening the file, with no build step, in a browser that reaches only Google Fonts and https://cdn.jsdelivr.net/npm/three@0.170.0/build/three.module.js.
answers:
[goal] 3D low-poly rebuild of the woodblock print in ./scene/index.html, with recording of what was taken from it in ./result.json.
[action] Read print.jpg through the image reader (AGY vision, since this model cannot see images). Found it is *The Great Wave off Kanagawa* (Kanagawa-oki Nami-ura / Fugaku Sanjūrokkei, Hokusai), 3 boats, snow-capped conical Mount Fuji. Built scene/index.html: single file, Three.js from the allowed CDN only, Google Fonts font. Giant curling indigo wave (bent shell + white crest claws) left, a smaller foreground curl, three oshiokuri-bune-style boats (7 huddled rowers each) at left-under-wave, lower center-right and back right, snow-capped Fuji mid-distance right, cream-to-grey-blue gradient sky, drifting clouds, instanced spray, low-poly ocean with vertex ripple, and gentle motion (wave sway, bobbing boats, camera sway). Verified in a headless browser: canvas renders (cream sky top, indigo ocean bottom, ~730 unique colors, no errors). Screenshot data could not be transmitted back to me, so visual confirmation is by pixel sampling, not by viewing. Closed the browser tabs.
[result] ./scene/index.html (opens with no build step) and ./result.json (boats: 3, mountain: Mount Fuji, palette and notes).
[next] Open scene/index.html in any browser to view; review against the print for composition/palette fidelity. Assumptions: "boats" counts the three oshiokuri-bune in the print; mountain named by the cartouche (Fugaku / Mount Fuji).
